facts.text: Started as an Assistant Professor of English and Humanities at Alfred State College, Aug 2023
Her film Young Monks was screened at the College English Conference hosted by Alfred State College, Oct 2025
Named Director of Services for the Rhode Island State Right to Life Committee, Jun 2026
Placed ninth in the girls 200-meter dash final in 29.55 seconds for Potsdam High School at the 2025 Peru Night Hawk Under the Lights Invitational
Named Top Graduate Anthropology Student by the College of Arts and Sciences at the University of Indianapolis, 2015
Co-authored a 2024 report on the 2024 field campaign at Susani - Gramurada de la Jupani in Romania, published in Ziridava. Studia Archaeologica
Named to SUNY Canton's Dean's List for Fall 2021 as a Nursing student
Named to SUNY Canton's Dean's List for Spring 2022 as a Bachelor of Science in Nursing student
Won the Women's Trap title at the 2026 USA Shooting Fall Selection Matches at Fort Carson and was named to the Trap National Team, Sep 2026
Joined the staff at Hillsdale College as an instructor and clay target range operator at the John Anthony Halter Shooting Sports Education Center, Oct 2023
Co-authored 'Measuring the impact of student success retention initiatives for engineering students at a private research university' in Frontiers in Education, Dec 2022
Co-authored a 2026 paper on Clarkson University's BOREALIS Scholars biomedical research training program for early-stage undergraduates in Biomedical Engineering Education, Mar 2026
Serves on the American Physical Society's Panel on Public Affairs for a term running January 1, 2024 to December 31, 2026

Earned her doctorate in physics at Montana State University in 2001, with a dissertation on superfluid effects on the thermal evolution and rotational dynamics of neutron stars supervised by Bennett Link
Her Midwife Sunday Wellness and Birth Center in Potsdam sponsored the $1,000 first-place award in the second annual St. Lawrence County Rotary Clubs Four-Way Test Essay Contest, 2026
Raised battery-storage fire-safety concerns at the Joint Legislative Public Hearing on the 2026 Executive Budget Proposal, citing the 2023 Lyme fire in his district
Lives outside Sackets Harbor, NY, with his family, 2026

note: PM run. Checked 75, filed 17 bullets across 11 people, each parent-verified on its source page and read back in the Sheet exactly once. Strongest: Summer Dorr started as an Assistant Professor of English and Humanities at Alfred State College in August 2023 (her blank companies field was filled with Alfred State College); Lydia Bartlett is Director of Services for the Rhode Island State Right to Life Committee (Rhode Island Catholic, June 2026); Aeriel Skinner won the Women's Trap title at the 2026 USA Shooting Fall Selection Matches and was named to the Trap National Team. Compounding lane (5 compounded): Kwadwo Appiah-Kubi's 2026 BOREALIS Scholars paper, Michelle Larson's American Physical Society Panel on Public Affairs term and her 2001 Montana State dissertation details, Sunday Wright Smith's birth-center sponsorship of the Rotary essay contest's $1,000 first-place award, and Mark Walczyk's battery-storage hearing comments; Walczyk's residence was also merged in the footprint text (NCPR says he lives outside Sackets Harbor; his record said Watertown, and the location field itself was not changed). Fresh sweep: none found - the only in-window directory items were already filed (Walczyk's re-election, Johnston's award, Evans's goals) or about non-directory people. The hot list carries Walczyk's Nov 4 re-election win only, inside its 48-hour window. Two batch claims were corrected before filing: both of Thea Krywanczyk's honors were reported as President's List, but section checks of the SUNY Canton pages put her name on the Dean's List both terms, and they were filed that way; a reported Marissa Wood conflict dissolved the same way (her Spring 2020 line is in the Dean's List section, matching her record), so nothing was filed for her.
